map.field.cropAcresBlock: Acres of it in this ~600 m block
map.field.perennialAcres: All tree, vine & berry acres in block
map.caveat.mineral: USGS mineral record: an occurrence or past mine, not proof of recoverable ore, access or safety. Old workings can be deadly.
map.caveat.well: State well record. Most are plugged or idle; never approach an unsealed well head.
map.caveat.fish: A past stocking record — it does not confirm fish are present now.
map.caveat.boat: Facility survey data; check current access.
map.caveat.dam: National Inventory of Dams record. Keep away from spillways and outlets — currents and sudden releases drown people.
map.caveat.surfaceWater: Surface water: filter, then boil or disinfect before drinking. Skip water with green scum or discolouration (toxic algae; boiling won’t remove it).
map.caveat.crops: USDA 2025 satellite crop map: usually right for big orchards, sometimes wrong for small ones. Trees and vines keep producing for decades but need water in dry regions and winter pruning. Private farmland — ask first.
map.caveat.pond: Small ponds are often livestock ponds with manure runoff: treat the water and cook any fish thoroughly. Small ponds can be fished out in weeks.
map.caveat.spring: Mapped spring — treat the water before drinking.
map.caveat.tap: Mapped tap; may be off in an emergency.

about.doesNot: What this guide does not do
about.doesNot.1: It points to original pages; the guides don’t write their own medical, chemical or electrical instructions. The assistant’s answers mark which sentences come from a cited page and which are its own wording.
about.doesNot.2: Nothing here replaces trained help. Each guide shows the sources’ own limits.
about.doesNot.3: Reading and watching are not the same as practising. Your ticks stay on this device.
about.doesNot.4: Shopping lists and carts in older reports are plans, not proof of supplies you own.
about.sourcesDetail: every publisher in this library, where it came from, and how to ask for something to be removed.
